title: Before It Has a Name
aliases: Only Colour, Not Yet a Flower
logline: In coconut country an hour inland from the sea, flowers grown for export are cut in the dark and graded under bulbs, and for about twenty minutes each morning the whole belt of shade houses turns from grey to colour before anything in it can be told apart.
human_question: What does the eye actually take in, before a thing is named at all?

place.what_kind_of_place: A belt of small growing places scattered through coconut smallholdings and low wet country an hour inland from the west coast: not one farm but dozens of them, a few hundred square metres each, tucked between houses and palms. Black shade netting stretched on poles, beds of anthurium and foliage underneath it, orchid benches, tanks and drip lines, a concrete-floored packing room with a bare bulb, boxes, sleeves, rubber bands, and a van that leaves before the roads fill. Outside the netting the country is coconut, scrub, a canal, a tar road, and more netting a few hundred metres further on.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because the best twenty minutes here are the ones where nothing can be identified. Before light there is a landscape of black net and grey shapes. Then colour arrives — not object by object, but everywhere at once, filling the whole frame while the individual flowers are still a mass — and only afterwards does anything become a particular thing. From the air the belt is a scatter of dark rectangles in coconut, which is an odd and beautiful pattern in its own right; and on the ground it is a place organised entirely around colour, where stock is put in lanes by shade long before anyone says a name out loud, and the names arrive last, printed on a carton.
place.what_moves_or_changes: Light, which is the whole subject and which arrives on its own schedule. The dispatch hour, which is fixed by a flight or a lorry and so pulls the whole morning earlier than anyone would choose. Weather, because shade netting is a way of arguing with the sun and rain settles what can be cut. Season and demand abroad, which decide what is in the beds at all. And the beds themselves, which are replanted, so a house that is solid colour one year is bare benches the next.
place.when_it_looks_best: The half hour on either side of first light, which is the film. A clear morning after rain, when the netting drips and the air is clean. Across the year, the weeks running up to whichever distant holiday the belt is packing for, when the houses are full and the packing room runs longest.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about light arriving in a place built to control it. Black netting in coconut country before dawn, torches, the sound of cutting, grey beds that become violently coloured over twenty minutes, hands under a bulb sorting by shade, boxes filling, a van leaving on an empty road, and the same country in full daylight looking like nothing in particular. It has a complete shape with nothing said over it: dark, arrival, colour, order, departure.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same twenty minutes become the sources’ plainest claim about seeing. The texts say the eye never meets a flower. It meets colour — a blend of the colours of many tiny clusters — and the knowing of it as this or that thing comes from marks laid down in earlier seeing [C036-P:L37–L41; C036-M:L9]. Here that order is not an argument; it is the working sequence of a morning. Colour arrives before anything is identifiable, the trade sorts by colour before it speaks a name, and the name itself turns up last, printed on the side of a box going somewhere else. The voice never claims that anyone here is deceived, and never says perception is an illusion — the sources are clear that colour is a real event, and only the assembled thing is a convention.

sequence.on_screen: Total dark, very high. A torch moving under netting, then two, then a scatter of them across the belt. Nothing has a colour.
sequence.voice: Nothing is getting in yet. The old texts are precise about this: the sensitive spot where sight actually lands is not the eye anybody can point to, and unless something strikes it hard enough to interrupt the mind’s resting state, there is no seeing at all [C035-P:L27].

sequence.on_screen: The twenty minutes, held in one rising shot: the belt of shade houses going from grey to colour, everywhere at once, while individual flowers are still a mass.
sequence.voice: Watch what arrives, and in what order. Colour is here before anything is anything.

sequence.on_screen: Inside a house at the moment colour separates: beds resolving into reds, whites, greens; still no shape you could name at this distance.
sequence.voice: The sources say the eye never meets a flower. It meets colour — on one account a blend of the colours of many tiny clusters — and the knowing of it as such-and-such a thing is added from marks laid down in earlier seeing [C036-P:L37–L41; C036-M:L9]. That is not a claim that you are being fooled. The colour is a real event. The flower is a convention laid over it.

sequence.on_screen: A packing room under one bulb: cut stems going into lanes by shade, hands moving fast, not a word spoken. Then sleeves, rubber bands, boxes.
sequence.voice: And the first moment of it carries no verdict. The sources call these bare sensing moments weak, needing an intact sensitivity, something to see, a medium such as light, and attention turned that way — and, for sight, they say the first feeling in it is neutral [C009-P:L85–L98; C009-P:L174–L176].

sequence.on_screen: A label printed and stuck on a carton: a variety name, a grade, a destination. The box closed. Stacked with others.
sequence.voice: The name arrives last, and it arrives from outside. Everything that happens after the colour — the grade, the price, the argument about the grade — belongs to a later part of the morning than the part the eye did.

sequence.on_screen: The van on an empty tar road in early light, then gone. Cut back to the belt from above in full daylight: dark rectangles in coconut, ordinary.
sequence.voice: The sources also say that the same sight can be identical for very different beings, and that the difference is entirely in what comes afterwards [C009-P:L85–L98]. What the eye did this morning was the same for everyone standing in that room.

sequence.on_screen: One flower, very close, in flat midday light, held far longer than is comfortable, until it stops looking like a flower.
sequence.voice: The old books give three sizes of now: the flash of a single event, the slightly longer stretch it takes to recognise something, and a whole life [C036-P:L45–L57]. This film has been about the second of those, and it lasted about twenty minutes.

concept_merge.why_together: C036 supplies the claim. Objects are of six kinds matched to the six doors, and the five sense doors take only present objects of their own kind [C036-P:L25–L31; C036-M:L5–L7]; the eye meets only colour, and the knowing of ‘I saw such-and-such a thing’ comes from marks learned in earlier seeing [C036-P:L37–L41; C036-M:L9]. It also supplies the film’s frame, the source’s three senses of ‘present’: the instant, the stretch it takes to recognise something, and a whole life [C036-P:L45–L57]. C035 supplies the threshold that makes the hour before dawn the subject rather than the setting: a door is not the visible organ but a fine sensitivity lodged in it, and nothing is experienced unless something strikes that sensitivity strongly enough to interrupt the resting mind [C035-P:L27]. C009 supplies what that first strike is like and what it is not: the bare sensing moments are weak, they need an intact sensitivity, an object, a medium such as light and attention, the same sight can be followed by completely different reactions in different beings, and for sight the first feeling is neutral [C009-P:L85–L98; C009-P:L174–L176]. A belt of growing houses where colour arrives before identity, and where a trade sorts by colour before it says a word, is those three claims running as a working morning.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the order we assume — see the thing, then notice its colour — is the wrong way round, and that a place exists where the true order is visible for about twenty minutes a day. C036 alone is a claim about what the eye touches. C035 alone is a claim about a threshold. C009 alone is a set of conditions and an absence of verdict. Together they let a viewer watch colour arrive with nothing attached to it, and then watch the names turn up afterwards, printed, from somewhere else — which is exactly the shape of the sources’ account and needs no one on screen to be a demonstration of anything.

concept_links.why: The digest gives the film its central claim: an object is whatever a mind takes hold of, the six kinds are matched to the six doors, and the five sense doors take only present objects of their own kind [C036-P:L25–L31; C036-M:L5–L7], while the eye meets only colour and the knowing of it as a particular thing comes from marks learned in earlier seeing [C036-P:L37–L41; C036-M:L9]. The three senses of ‘present’ — the instant, the stretch it takes to recognise something, and a whole life [C036-P:L45–L57] — give the film its shape and its last beat. Two things in the digest are held to exactly. Its guard that ‘perception is an illusion’ distorts the text is written into the voice: colour is a real event for the source, and only the assembled, named thing is a convention. And the digest’s note that the Pradeepika calls the visible object ‘unmixed’ in one place [C036-P:L61] and a blend of many clusters’ colours in another [C036-P:L41] without reconciling them is left open on screen rather than resolved. The digest’s other limits are simply kept off the film: no ‘live in the present moment’ advice, since the source states a fact about the senses rather than giving counsel; no presentation of the traditional account of how sound and smell travel as acoustics or physics; nothing from the deathbed-object teaching; and no use of the ranking of which minds take which objects as any kind of measure of people.

The digest separates the organ you can point to from the fine sensitivity lodged in it, and says experience only gets in where something strikes that sensitivity strongly enough to interrupt the mind’s resting state, so having eyes open is not yet seeing [C035-P:L27]. The hour before light in a place whose whole business is colour is the condition under which that threshold is the working problem of a trade rather than a doctrine. The digest’s limits are carried without exception. The sensitivity is not the retina and is never narrated as anatomy; the Margaya’s ‘size of a louse’s head’ spot where images fall [C035-M:L9] is reported tradition and does not appear as fact. The mind-door is a moment of mind and not the brain. The extracts are a descriptive classification and not a ‘guard your senses’ slogan, so the film gives no advice about what to look at. And the phrase ‘doors of perception’, with its literary and psychedelic freight, is not used anywhere.

The digest describes the bare rootless moments of sensing as weak, sets out the conditions each one needs — an intact sensitivity, an object, a medium such as light or air, and attention turned that way — and shows that the same sight can be followed by quite different reactions in different beings, reactions that belong to a later stage [C009-P:L85–L98]; it also records that except for touch these moments carry only neutral feeling [C009-P:L174–L176]. That is why this film can put a whole trade’s excitement, money and argument on the far side of the bare arrival of colour. The digest’s prohibitions are load-bearing. ‘Rootless’ is not ‘uncaused’ [C009-M:L3], and the voice never suggests the morning happens for no reason. The source’s treatment of pleasant and unpleasant contact as the result of past action is never turned into anyone on camera deserving what they have. The Pradeepika’s link between very weak wholesome action and rebirth with blindness or deafness [C009-P:L168–L172] is a doctrinal claim about rebirth and is kept out of the film in every form. The neutral first feeling is not the modern line that a person chooses how they feel, and it does not mean the world looks bland — a film made of violent colour is the right place to say so.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That colour arrives before identity does, and that the naming, the grading and the valuing are all added afterwards from what has been seen before. Nobody is being fooled by this and nothing is an illusion; it is simply that the part we credit to the eye is much smaller and much earlier than it feels, and almost everything we think we saw was supplied from somewhere else.
what_must_be_real: The growers’ own hour. Nothing is cut, lit, sorted or packed for the camera, and the dispatch is not delayed for a shot; if the light is wrong on the morning the crew is there, that is the morning they have. No artificial light is added to the beds and no colour is pushed in the grade, because the film’s only claim is about what the light actually does. No person on screen is presented as the one who sees or judges — that is the precise thing this group’s concepts deny, and the grading here is shown as hands, lanes and boxes rather than as anybody’s perception. These are small private holdings beside people’s houses, so every house filmed is filmed by agreement, and no grower’s prices, buyers or yields go on screen without their consent.
position_hint: early: it is the group’s cleanest statement that bare sensing comes before naming, and the later films about order, response and lingering assume it. It should come after the film about turning toward and before the ones about what happens further down the line.
risks: Letting the film say that perception is an illusion, which the digest names as a distortion: colour, sound and smell are real events for the source, and only the named thing is a convention.
Turning the sources’ statement that the senses meet only the present into ‘live in the present moment’ advice. The digest is explicit that the text describes rather than counsels.
Narrating the sense-sensitivity as the retina, or the Margaya’s ‘size of a louse’s head’ spot [C035-M:L9] as anatomy.
Using the phrase ‘doors of perception’, which the digest tells the series to avoid, or letting the film become a ‘guard your senses’ argument.
Presenting a grower or grader as the one who sees, or reading a decision off somebody’s face. A camera cannot show a mind-moment and the group denies a separate seer.
Treating ‘rootless’ as ‘random’ or ‘uncaused’, which the digest corrects directly [C009-M:L3].
Letting the source’s account of pleasant and unpleasant contact as a result of past action reach the screen as anyone deserving their circumstances.
Carrying the Pradeepika’s link between weak wholesome action and rebirth with blindness or deafness [C009-P:L168–L172] into the film in any form.
Letting the neutral first feeling be heard as either ‘you choose how you feel’ or ‘the world is bland’, when it is a technical claim about a first instant.

Quietly resolving the source’s own unreconciled description of the visible object as ‘unmixed’ in one place [C036-P:L61] and as a blend of many clusters’ colours in another [C036-P:L41]. The film leaves it open.
Becoming an export-industry film, or a piece about cut-flower economics, chemical use or air freight. Those are real subjects and none of them is this one.
Adding light, grading the colour up, or shooting the arrival of colour in a way that is achieved in post rather than by the morning.
drop_if: The growers will not have a crew in their houses before dawn, which is a reasonable thing to refuse.
Cutting and grading turn out to happen entirely under artificial light in closed rooms, so the arrival of colour is never the working condition and the film has no subject.
It can only be made by asking anyone to cut, sort or pack at a time that suits the camera.

connections.note: Two films about a threshold of light: one where a lamp decides how far the world extends, one where dawn decides when colour begins.
The same claim at two doors: what arrives as bare smell before it is named, and what arrives as bare colour before it is named.

selection.reason: It is the group’s clearest case of bare sensing preceding the name, and the twenty minutes that carry the argument are also the most beautiful footage the place produces.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-22 into the footage-led shape. The market is dropped: the slate already carries a night wholesale terminal and a weekly fair, and a third trading floor would have repeated both. The concept is kept exactly — bare colour arriving before the name does — and moved to the growing and gathering end, where the arrival of colour is a daily physical event rather than a metaphor for one, and where the name genuinely turns up last, printed on a carton. Concepts re-read from the digests and every citation re-verified against digest evidence.

suggested_location.name: The floriculture smallholdings around Divulapitiya, in the coconut country of the northern Gampaha district

also_known_as.name: cut foliage
also_known_as.meaning: leaves and stems grown and exported for their shape and colour rather than for flowers

suggested_location.region: Gampaha district, Western Province: the low, wet coconut country inland of the coast road and north of the Kelani valley
suggested_location.why_here: It is a whole working belt rather than one farm, it is organised entirely around colour, and it is not a market. Floriculture in this country is concentrated in this district, and this town in particular is a recognised centre of it, with over a hundred people in the trade and an export-orientated flower village arranged around them. That means dozens of small shade-net houses scattered through coconut smallholdings, all cutting in the same hour for the same dispatch — which gives the film both its aerial pattern and its one unrepeatable shot, the twenty minutes in which a landscape of grey netting turns to solid colour before anything in it can be told apart. And because it is the growing end and not the selling end, the names really do arrive last, printed on a box.
what_to_film: The arrival of colour, in one unbroken rising shot over the belt, from black netting to full colour, timed so that nothing is identifiable for as long as possible.
The same twenty minutes from inside one house at bed level, so that the colour separates out around the camera rather than below it.
The belt from high above in flat daylight: dark rectangles scattered through coconut, an odd and legible pattern.
Cutting in the dark by torch — sound, hands, stems — with almost nothing visible.
A packing room under one bulb: stock going into lanes by shade, fast, with no names spoken.
The label: printed, stuck, the box closed and stacked. The first time a word appears in the film.
The van leaving on an empty road, and the roads filling behind it.
One flower held very close in flat midday light for much longer than is comfortable.
suggested_location.access: By road; the belt is spread through ordinary village and smallholding country and the houses sit beside people’s homes. Everything depends on individual growers agreeing, and on being there at their hour rather than asking them to move it. Low-light flight before dawn over inhabited smallholdings needs both the growers’ agreement and whatever permissions apply locally, and is the part of the plan most likely to fail.
suggested_location.best_time: The half hour either side of first light, which is the whole film. A clear morning after overnight rain. Across the year, the run-up to whichever export holiday the belt is packing for, when the houses are fullest and the packing rooms run longest.

suggested_location.research_note: That floriculture in this country is concentrated in the Western Province with this district in the forefront, that over five hundred hectares are under it there, that this particular town is a recognised centre with more than a hundred people engaged in the trade and an export-orientated flower village arranged for it, and that the export range runs to orchids, anthurium, gerbera, chrysanthemum and cut foliage sent to Europe, Japan and the Gulf are from the sources above and are desk research only. The coordinates are an open mapping database point for the town, not for any grower. No specific holding has been identified, nobody has been approached, and the working pattern assumed here — cutting in the dark, grading under a bulb, dispatch before the roads fill — is inferred from the perishability of the crop and the export schedule rather than confirmed for this belt. None of the three images is of a growing site: two are of the surrounding district and one is of the flower type photographed elsewhere in the country. Each caption says so.

unknowns: Whether cutting and grading here actually happen before dawn, or whether the crop is cut later in the day, is unverified and decides whether the film exists.
No grower has been identified or approached, and the belt is made of private holdings beside people’s houses.
Whether the houses are close enough together for the belt to read as a pattern from the air has not been checked.
Low-light drone flight over inhabited smallholdings before dawn may not be permissible, and it carries the film’s single most important shot.
Whether enough of the grading happens in daylight or open-sided rooms for the arrival of colour to be the real working condition, rather than a closed room under a bulb, is unknown.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
